title: Strict decrease in the unmarked count
statement: Let $b,K$ be natural numbers and let $M,M':\mathbb Z\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$ be markings of integer cells. Suppose every cell marked by $M$ is also marked by $M'$, and the two markings agree at every cell other than the cells $b,b+1,\ldots,b+K-1$. If $M'\ne M$, then the number of unmarked cells in this finite range is strictly smaller for $M'$ than for $M$.
hypotheses_covered: Every cell marked by $M$ is marked by $M'$
The markings agree outside the cells $b$ through $b+K-1$
